messages:
sanjay: Heads-up — Alert from CloudTrail anomaly detector: a CI role appears to have a KMS key policy with a wildcard principal. saw a recent PutKeyPolicy from our CI account. not good.
security-oncall: Ack. marking P1 and paging infra. can you paste the exact policy snippet?
sanjay: here's the relevant change from CloudTrail: 
```json
{"Action":"kms:Decrypt","Principal":"*","Effect":"Allow","Resource":"arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01"}
```
security-oncall: that Principal:* is definitely a misconfig. could be accidental template render bug in our terraform module.
morgan: on it. immediate containment plan: 1) detach the policy from key 2) add a deny to the CI role to use kms:Decrypt 3) enable key rotation / create new key and rotate materials.
katy: agree. also enable CloudTrail Insights for the account and start a targeted CloudWatch Logs query for KMS API calls in the last 48h. need to know if any ciphertext was decrypted by an external actor.
nate: I'm going to block the CI role from assuming cross-account roles until we confirm. running: 
```bash
aws iam update-role --role-name ci-deploy-role --description "temporarily disabled for KMS incident"
aws iam put-role-policy --role-name ci-deploy-role --policy-document file://deny-kms.json
```
(deny-kms.json = deny kms:Decrypt on arn:aws:kms:... for all principals)
security-oncall: also rotate any long-lived keys that the CI system uses for deployments. tag affected resources with `incident/1769001234`.
sanjay: initial query shows 3 Decrypt calls in past 2 hours from the CI role itself — looks like CI used the access as expected. no unknown principals observed so far.
morgan: good, that suggests not exfil. still we need to tighten the key policy and patch terraform. I'm pushing a hotfix to the kms module to not template '*' for Principal.
katy: I'll run re-encryption plan: create new CMK (customer-managed key) with stricter key policy limiting to specific ARNs, re-encrypt S3 objects using aws s3 cp + --sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id <new-key> or use KMS re-encrypt API.
nate: CI credentials were rotated 15m ago as precaution. I'm also revoking any temporary sessions with: 
```bash
aws sts revoke-session --session-id <session>
# (using internal tooling to revoke tokens)
```
security-oncall: please add audit entries to the incident tracker and notify our SOC feed. also open a compliance ticket for KMS policy review: ticket CORP-4821.
sanjay: quick note — found terraform diff: our module allowed var.allowed_principals default = "*" when ephemeral. pushing patch to change default to empty list and require explicit principals. creating PR now.
morgan: PR look good. will merge after one more reviewer. after merge we need to run a drift detection sweep and apply fixes to prod key policies.
katy: post-containment checklist for ops: 
- rotate CMK -> done in my branch
- re-encrypt critical buckets -> pending (start in 30m)
- enable KMS key policy guardrails in policygen -> pending
- update terraform module + run `terraform plan` across accounts -> pending

nate: communicating to platform teams: "Do not add wildcard principals to key policies. If you need broad access, use IAM roles with explicit ARNs and KMS grants." sending now.
security-oncall: we should also add an audit rule to detect PutKeyPolicy events that include Principal:"*" and auto-create a ticket. adding to the SOC ruleset.
sanjay: thanks everyone. small win: no external decryption found, no suspicious egress. continuing containment and will follow up with a short postmortem tomorrow 09:30 PT. :white_check_mark:
morgan: adding a short blameless postmortem draft to docs and will include remediation owners.
deploy-bot: role ci-deploy-role detached from key abcd-ef01 at 1769001456.
security-oncall: closing the active page for now — remain on-call until 09:30 PT tomorrow for any regressions. incident channel: #inc-1769001234 (created).
